correctness.rationale: The path-extension formula counts all completions; separate deletion formulas yield exact off-path and endpoint leaf probabilities and n=k+1 boundary. Algebra proves cubic forward difference and modes. Centered regression is positive then negative around unconditional mean, proving exact strict negative covariance. The distance distribution has Gaussian tails and Rayleigh scaling; a uniform conditional-mean expansion with controlled tails gives the precise covariance coefficient; Prüfer factorial moments give variance and correlation. The standalone checker exhaustively reconstructs 280391 trees through n=8 and 15931 exact rational forward differences; three larger numerical tests agree. Finite computations are corroboration.

originality.rationale: The classical labeled-forest extension lemma and degree/distance marginal laws are explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. Direct inspection of Pitman’s forest-counting argument, Aldous–Pitman’s accessible tree-structure analysis, and the complete published conditional endpoint-degree result does not give the global-leaf regression, cubic-root conditional maximum, or strict finite covariance with sharp coefficient. The endpoint-degree theorem treats one fixed vertex and exhibits decreasing rather than unimodal regression; it does not determine the off-path leaves. Search cannot prove uniqueness; an older implicit multivariate enumerator remains a residual risk.
